about: Every settings row the interface can show, made by ps5/tools/settings-inventory.py from the code (ps5/tests/bigpicture/inventory). The no-loss test compares the code with this file; bless writes it.

rows.heading: BEHAVIOUR
rows.label: Settings Shown
rows.desc: Determines how many settings are shown. More adds finer options; Everything shows every option, including ones that can stop games from working.

rows.heading: BEHAVIOUR
rows.label: Pause On Controller Disconnection
rows.desc: Pauses the emulator when a controller with bindings is disconnected.

rows.heading: BEHAVIOUR
rows.label: Warn About Unsafe Settings
rows.desc: Displays warnings when settings are enabled which may break games.

rows.heading: BEHAVIOUR
rows.label: Swap OK/Cancel
rows.desc: Swaps the Cross and Circle buttons in all menus, as on Japanese consoles.

rows.heading: APPEARANCE
rows.label: Skin
rows.desc: Changes the colors and style of the interface. Carbon uses a black background, which suits OLED screens.

choices.name: Chakra (Modern and Accessible, after Chakra UI)
Humane (Clean and Readable, after Semantic UI)

rows.heading: APPEARANCE
rows.label: Accent Color
rows.desc: Selects the color used to highlight the selected item and enabled options.

rows.heading: APPEARANCE
rows.label: Background
rows.desc: Selects what is shown behind the menus: a still or animated background, the selected game's artwork, or your pictures from the "backgrounds" folder.

rows.heading: APPEARANCE
rows.label: Picture Duration
rows.desc: Determines how long each of your background pictures is shown before the next one.

rows.heading: APPEARANCE
rows.label: Picture Dimming
rows.desc: Darkens your background pictures so the text on top of them stays readable.

rows.heading: APPEARANCE
rows.label: Reload Pictures
rows.code_label: My pictures: look into the folder again
rows.desc: Checks the "backgrounds" folder again for new pictures.

rows.heading: APPEARANCE
rows.label: Motion
rows.desc: Controls how much the interface animates. All animates the background and slides the menus; Less only fades; None disables animation.

rows.heading: APPEARANCE
rows.label: Startup Animation
rows.desc: Plays the animated logo on startup. Press any button to skip it.

rows.heading: APPEARANCE
rows.label: Startup Animation Style
rows.desc: Selects which of the four startup animations plays. Random picks a different one each time.

rows.heading: APPEARANCE
rows.label: Interface Size
rows.desc: Makes the whole interface smaller so more fits on screen.

rows.heading: APPEARANCE
rows.label: Text Size
rows.desc: Makes the text larger or smaller without changing the rest of the interface.

rows.heading: APPEARANCE
rows.label: High Contrast
rows.desc: Makes text brighter and outlines stronger.

rows.heading: APPEARANCE
rows.label: Color Blind Mode
rows.desc: Uses blue and orange instead of green and red to show success and failure.

rows.heading: APPEARANCE
rows.label: Startup Video
rows.desc: Plays a short video on startup in place of the startup animation, at the startup sound's volume. Requires Startup Animation enabled and Motion set to All.

rows.heading: SOUND
rows.label: Interface Sounds
rows.desc: Plays sounds when moving and selecting in the menus.

rows.heading: SOUND
rows.label: Interface Sound Volume
rows.desc: Controls the volume of the interface sounds.

rows.heading: SOUND
rows.label: Menu Music
rows.desc: Plays the music files in the "music" folder (WAV, MP3, OGG or FLAC) in the menus.

rows.heading: SOUND
rows.label: Menu Music Volume
rows.desc: Controls the volume of the menu music.

rows.heading: SOUND
rows.label: Music Order
rows.desc: Determines the order in which the music files are played.

rows.heading: SOUND
rows.label: Next Track
rows.desc: Skips to the next music file.

rows.heading: SOUND
rows.label: Startup Sound
rows.desc: Plays a sound with the startup animation. A "startup.wav" in the title folder replaces it.

rows.heading: SOUND
rows.label: Startup Sound Volume
rows.desc: Controls the volume of the startup sound and video.

rows.heading: CARE FOR THE SCREEN
rows.label: Dim When Idle
rows.code_label: Go dark when nothing is pressed
rows.desc: Dims the screen after this long without input, then turns it black. Press any button to wake it.

rows.heading: CARE FOR THE SCREEN
rows.label: Screen Saver
rows.code_label: Then the black screen with the mark
rows.desc: Shows a black screen with a moving logo after the screen dims. When disabled, the screen only dims.

rows.heading: CARE FOR THE SCREEN
rows.label: Pixel Shift
rows.desc: Moves the whole picture by a few pixels every couple of minutes to reduce the risk of burn-in on OLED screens.

rows.heading: CARE FOR THE SCREEN
rows.label: Fade Button Hints
rows.desc: Fades the button hints at the bottom of the screen when nothing has been pressed for a while.

rows.heading: CARE FOR THE SCREEN
rows.label: Dim Game When Idle
rows.code_label: Darken the game when nothing is pressed
rows.desc: Dims the game after this long without input. Press any button to bring it back.

rows.heading: GAME SCANNING
rows.label: Scan For New Games
rows.desc: Identifies any new files added to the game directories.

rows.heading: GAME SCANNING
rows.label: Rescan All Games
rows.desc: Forces a full rescan of all games previously identified.

rows.heading: THE LIST
rows.label: Library View
rows.desc: Selects how games are shown in the library. The touch pad also switches views.

rows.heading: THE LIST
rows.label: Show Gameplay Background
rows.code_label: A picture of play behind the shelves
rows.desc: Shows a screenshot of the selected game behind the shelves.

rows.heading: THE LIST
rows.label: Group Multi-Disc Games
rows.code_label: Group the discs of a game
rows.desc: Shows a game that has several discs as one entry, which starts from the disc played last.

rows.heading: THE LIST
rows.label: Prefer English Game Titles
rows.desc: For games with both a title in the game's native language and one in English, prefer the English title. Affects how game titles are displayed in the game list.

rows.heading: THE LIST
rows.label: Download Game Pictures
rows.desc: Downloads title screens and screenshots for your games from libretro's thumbnail collection.

rows.heading: WHERE GAMES ARE
rows.label: Search USB Drives
rows.desc: Shows the games in a "Crux2" or "PS2" folder on a USB drive in the game list.

rows.heading: WHERE GAMES ARE
rows.label: Search Disc Drives
rows.desc: Checks the console's disc drive and USB DVD drives for PS2 discs and shows them on a tab of their own. USB DVD drives can also read PS2 CDs.

rows.heading: WHERE GAMES ARE
rows.label: Cache Disc in Memory
rows.code_label: Read the disc into memory while playing
rows.desc: Copies the whole disc into memory while playing, so the drive is no longer needed. When disabled, only recently read data is kept.

rows.heading: WHERE GAMES ARE
rows.label: Keep Disc Spinning
rows.desc: Reads from the disc every 20 seconds so the drive does not spin down during play.

rows.heading: WHERE GAMES ARE
rows.label: Create Disc Image
rows.code_label: Make an image of the disc
rows.desc: Copies the disc to an ISO, CHD or CSO image on the console, a USB drive or a network share.

rows.heading: WHERE GAMES ARE
rows.label: Eject Disc
rows.desc: Unlocks and opens a disc drive's tray.

rows.heading: WHERE GAMES ARE
rows.label: Sync Covers
rows.desc: Syncs covers both ways with the backup location, so every device that uses it has them.

rows.heading: FROM THE INTERNET
rows.label: Download Covers Automatically
rows.desc: Downloads missing covers from libretro's thumbnail collection after each scan, and from the ps2-covers collection for games it has none for.

rows.heading: FROM THE INTERNET
rows.label: Download Game Pictures Automatically
rows.desc: Downloads title screens and screenshots for your games after each scan.

rows.heading: FROM THE INTERNET
rows.label: Show Game Descriptions
rows.code_label: Look up what each game is
rows.desc: Shows a short description of the game in the drive, looked up on Wikipedia.

rows.heading: FROM THE INTERNET
rows.label: Refresh Game Descriptions
rows.desc: Clears the stored game descriptions so they are looked up again.

rows.heading: FROM THE INTERNET
rows.label: Download Missing Covers
rows.desc: Downloads covers for every game that has none.

rows.heading: FROM THE INTERNET
rows.label: Download Cheats for All Games
rows.desc: Downloads cheats for all your games from the cheat collections on GitHub. Cheats stay disabled until they are enabled for a game.

rows.heading: FROM THE INTERNET
rows.label: Download Game Patches
rows.desc: Downloads PCSX2's game patches (widescreen, no-interlacing, 60 FPS and more) from GitHub.

rows.heading: GAME FOLDERS
rows.label: Add Search Directory
rows.desc: Adds a new directory to the game search list.

rows.heading: GAME FOLDERS
rows.label: /mnt/usb0/games
rows.desc: Removes this game folder from the game list when pressed: its games leave the library, and the files stay where they are.

rows.heading: A NEW SHARE
rows.label: Protocol
rows.desc: Selects SMB for a Windows PC and most NAS, or NFS for a NAS or a Linux PC that shares its folders that way.

rows.heading: A NEW SHARE
rows.label: Server
rows.desc: Selects the PC or NAS: one found on this network (answering on the SMB or NFS port), its address entered on the number pad, or its name typed in.

rows.heading: A NEW SHARE
rows.label: Share and Folder
rows.desc: Selects the share and the folder in it that holds the games, for example Games/PS2, from the server's list or typed in.

rows.heading: A NEW SHARE
rows.label: Name
rows.desc: Sets how the share is shown in the library. When left empty, its last folder's name is used.

rows.heading: A NEW SHARE
rows.label: User
rows.desc: Sets an account for this share only. When left empty, the default share account is used (guest for an open share).

rows.heading: A NEW SHARE
rows.label: Password
rows.desc: Sets the password of this share's account.

rows.heading: A NEW SHARE
rows.label: Test Share
rows.desc: Connects to the share and reads its folder, and reports what failed if it cannot: the address, the port, the account, the share's name or the folder. Nothing is saved.

rows.heading: A NEW SHARE
rows.label: Add Share
rows.desc: Connects to the share, adds its games to the library and keeps it in "network.cfg" for future sessions.

rows.heading: A NEW SHARE
rows.label: Cancel
rows.desc: Discards the changes to the share.

rows.heading: NETWORK SHARES
rows.label: Add Network Share
rows.desc: Adds a folder of games on a PC or NAS, read over the network as the games play (SMB or NFS). Set up with the on-screen keyboard and number pad; "network.cfg" is written automatically.

rows.heading: NETWORK SHARES
rows.label: Default Share Account
rows.desc: Sets the user and password for the SMB shares that have no account of their own. Use "guest" and no password for an open share.

rows.heading: WHERE CRUX2 KEEPS ITS FILES
rows.label: BIOS Directory
rows.desc: Changes the folder used for BIOS images in future sessions, or restores the default.

rows.heading: WHERE CRUX2 KEEPS ITS FILES
rows.label: Memory Cards Directory
rows.desc: Changes the folder used for memory cards in future sessions, or restores the default.

rows.heading: WHERE CRUX2 KEEPS ITS FILES
rows.label: Save States Directory
rows.desc: Changes the folder used for save states in future sessions, or restores the default.

rows.heading: WHERE CRUX2 KEEPS ITS FILES
rows.label: Snapshots Directory
rows.desc: Changes the folder used for screenshots and GS dumps in future sessions, or restores the default.

rows.heading: WHERE CRUX2 KEEPS ITS FILES
rows.label: Cheats Directory
rows.desc: Changes the folder used for cheats in future sessions, or restores the default.

rows.heading: WHERE CRUX2 KEEPS ITS FILES
rows.label: Covers Directory
rows.desc: Changes the folder used for covers in future sessions, or restores the default.

rows.heading: WHERE CRUX2 KEEPS ITS FILES
rows.label: Texture Replacements Directory
rows.desc: Changes the folder used for replacement textures in future sessions, or restores the default.

rows.heading: THE PLAYSTATION 2'S OWN MENU
rows.label: Start BIOS
rows.desc: Start the console without any disc inserted.

rows.heading: BIOS SELECTION
rows.label: BIOS Selection
rows.desc: Changes the BIOS image used to start future sessions.

rows.heading: BIOS SELECTION
rows.label: Use Open-Source BIOS
rows.code_label: Free BIOS when none of my own is found
rows.desc: Uses OpenPS2BIOS, an open-source BIOS that comes with the title, when no BIOS image is found. Many games do not get past their menus with it.

rows.heading: LANGUAGE
rows.label: Console Language
rows.desc: Sets the language games are told the PS2 uses. Many European games use it to choose their language. The BIOS's own settings are not changed.

rows.heading: OPTIONS AND PATCHES
rows.label: Fast Boot
rows.desc: Patches the BIOS to skip the console's boot animation.

rows.heading: OPTIONS AND PATCHES
rows.label: Fast Forward Boot
rows.desc: Removes emulation speed throttle until the game starts to reduce startup time.

rows.heading: SPEED CONTROL
rows.label: Normal Speed
rows.desc: Sets the speed when running without fast forwarding.

rows.heading: SPEED CONTROL
rows.label: Fast-Forward Speed
rows.desc: Sets the speed when using the fast forward hotkey.

rows.heading: SPEED CONTROL
rows.label: Slow-Motion Speed
rows.desc: Sets the speed when using the slow motion hotkey.

rows.heading: SYSTEM SETTINGS
rows.label: EE Cycle Rate
rows.desc: Underclocks or overclocks the emulated Emotion Engine CPU.

rows.heading: SYSTEM SETTINGS
rows.label: EE Cycle Skipping
rows.desc: Makes the emulated Emotion Engine skip cycles. Helps a small subset of games like SOTC. Most of the time it's harmful to performance.

rows.heading: SYSTEM SETTINGS
rows.label: Enable Multithreaded VU1 (MTVU)
rows.desc: Generally a speedup on CPUs with 4 or more cores. Safe for most games, but a few are incompatible and may hang.

rows.heading: SYSTEM SETTINGS
rows.label: Thread Pinning
rows.desc: Determines how the emulator's threads are placed on the CPU cores. Unpinned suits most games; try another option if a game is slow at every resolution.

rows.heading: SYSTEM SETTINGS
rows.label: Dedicated Graphics Driver Core
rows.code_label: Graphics driver on a core of its own
rows.desc: With Dedicated Cores, moves the graphics driver's thread off the GS thread's core, so the GS thread has a core to itself. May reduce performance in some games.

rows.heading: SYSTEM SETTINGS
rows.label: Driver Core Kept Free
rows.desc: With the graphics driver on a core of its own, keeps the emulator's other threads off that core.

rows.heading: SYSTEM SETTINGS
rows.label: Enable Fast CDVD
rows.desc: Fast disc access, shorter loading times. Check HDLoader compatibility lists for games that are known to have issues with this.

rows.heading: SYSTEM SETTINGS
rows.label: Enable CDVD Precaching
rows.code_label: Load the whole disc into memory
rows.desc: Loads the disc image into RAM before starting the virtual machine.

rows.heading: SYSTEM SETTINGS
rows.label: Enable Cheats
rows.desc: Enables loading cheats from pnach files.

rows.heading: SYSTEM SETTINGS
rows.label: Enable Host Filesystem
rows.desc: Allows games and homebrew to access files / folders directly on the host computer.

rows.heading: FRAME PACING / LATENCY CONTROL
rows.label: Refresh Rate
rows.desc: Selects the refresh rate sent to the TV. 120 Hz requires a TV that supports it and is needed for frame generation to 120 FPS and black frame insertion. Holding L1 and R1 during startup uses 60 Hz once.

rows.heading: FRAME PACING / LATENCY CONTROL
rows.label: Variable Refresh Rate (VRR)
rows.desc: At 120 Hz on a TV that supports VRR, shows each frame as soon as it is ready instead of at the next fixed refresh. Smoother when a game runs below full speed.

rows.heading: FRAME PACING / LATENCY CONTROL
rows.label: Frame Pacing
rows.desc: Determines how frames are paced. Host VSync paces frames by the display's refresh for the smoothest motion; Internal Timing paces them by the emulator's clock, for games whose frame rate the display cannot match.

rows.heading: FRAME PACING / LATENCY CONTROL
rows.label: Maximum Frame Latency
rows.desc: Sets the number of frames which can be queued.

rows.heading: FRAME PACING / LATENCY CONTROL
rows.label: Queue Frames When Slow
rows.code_label: Queue frames while the game is behind
rows.desc: When a game runs below full speed, allows up to 2 frames to be queued so the emulator and the GS thread can work at the same time. Can increase input lag while the game is slow.

rows.heading: FRAME PACING / LATENCY CONTROL
rows.label: Advanced Frame Display
rows.code_label: Show a frame as it begins
rows.desc: Displays the newest frame immediately at the beginning of the frame raster time, instead of at the end. Can reduce perceived input lag, but may cause problems with some games, such as Soulcalibur II and Baldur's Gate Dark Alliance II.

rows.heading: FRAME PACING / LATENCY CONTROL
rows.label: Skip Presenting Duplicate Frames
rows.desc: Skips displaying frames that don't change in 25/30fps games. Can improve speed, but increase input lag/make frame pacing worse.

rows.heading: FRAME PACING / LATENCY CONTROL
rows.label: Black Frame Insertion
rows.desc: Inserts a black frame after each frame at 120 Hz to reduce motion blur. Makes the picture darker. Cannot be combined with frame generation.

rows.heading: ACCURATE FLOATING POINT
rows.label: Accurate FPU Floating Point
rows.desc: Emulates the FPU's floating-point math exactly as the PS2 does, for games whose physics or AI go wrong otherwise. Reduces performance. Enabled automatically for the games known to need it.

rows.heading: ACCURATE FLOATING POINT
rows.label: Accurate VU0 Floating Point
rows.desc: Emulates VU0's floating-point math exactly as the PS2 does. Usually needed together with the FPU option. Reduces performance. Enabled automatically for the games known to need it.

rows.heading: ACCURATE FLOATING POINT
rows.label: Accurate VU1 Floating Point
rows.desc: Emulates VU1's floating-point math exactly as the PS2 does, which fixes some graphical errors. Greatly reduces performance.

rows.heading: REAL-TIME CLOCK
rows.label: Manually Set Real-Time Clock
rows.desc: Manually set a real-time clock to use for the virtual PlayStation 2 instead of using your OS' system clock.

rows.heading: REAL-TIME CLOCK
rows.label: Year
rows.desc: Calendar year for the virtual PS2 RTC.

rows.heading: REAL-TIME CLOCK
rows.label: Month
rows.desc: Month of the year (1-12).

rows.heading: REAL-TIME CLOCK
rows.label: Day
rows.desc: Day of the month (1-31).

rows.heading: REAL-TIME CLOCK
rows.label: Hour
rows.desc: Hour of the day (0-23).

rows.heading: REAL-TIME CLOCK
rows.label: Minute
rows.desc: Minute of the hour (0-59).

rows.heading: REAL-TIME CLOCK
rows.label: Second
rows.desc: Second of the minute (0-59).

rows.heading: PATCHES
rows.label: A patch
rows.desc: What the patch does.

rows.heading: CHEATS
rows.label: A cheat
rows.desc: What the cheat does.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: FPU Multiply Hack
rows.desc: For Tales of Destiny.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: Use Software Renderer For FMVs
rows.desc: Needed for some games with complex FMV rendering.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: Skip MPEG Hack
rows.desc: Skips videos/FMVs in games to avoid game hanging/freezes.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: Preload TLB Hack
rows.desc: To avoid TLB miss on Goemon.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: EE Timing Hack
rows.desc: General-purpose timing hack. Known to affect following games: Digital Devil Saga, SSX.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: Instant DMA Hack
rows.desc: Good for cache emulation problems. Known to affect following games: Fire Pro Wrestling Z.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: OPH Flag Hack
rows.desc: Known to affect following games: Bleach Blade Battlers, Growlanser II and III, Wizardry.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: Emulate GIF FIFO
rows.desc: Correct but slower. Known to affect the following games: FIFA Street 2.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: DMA Busy Hack
rows.desc: Known to affect following games: Mana Khemia 1, Metal Saga, Pilot Down Behind Enemy Lines.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: Delay VIF1 Stalls
rows.desc: For SOCOM 2 HUD and Spy Hunter loading hang.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: Emulate VIF FIFO
rows.desc: Simulate VIF1 FIFO read ahead. Known to affect following games: Test Drive Unlimited, Transformers.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: Full VU0 Synchronization
rows.desc: Forces tight VU0 sync on every COP2 instruction.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: VU I Bit Hack
rows.desc: Avoids constant recompilation in some games. Known to affect the following games: Scarface The World is Yours, Crash Tag Team Racing.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: VU Add Hack
rows.desc: For Tri-Ace Games: Star Ocean 3, Radiata Stories, Valkyrie Profile 2.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: VU Overflow Hack
rows.desc: To check for possible float overflows (Superman Returns).

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: VU Sync
rows.desc: Run behind. To avoid sync problems when reading or writing VU registers.

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: VU XGKick Sync
rows.desc: Use accurate timing for VU XGKicks (slower).

rows.heading: GAME FIXES (SET BY ITSELF FOR KNOWN GAMES)
rows.label: Force Blit Internal FPS Detection
rows.desc: Use alternative method to calculate internal FPS to avoid false readings in some games.

rows.heading: CHEATS
rows.label: Enable Cheats
rows.desc: Enables loading cheats from pnach files.

rows.heading: CHEATS
rows.label: Show Cheats For All CRCs
rows.code_label: Those of other versions of the game too
rows.desc: Toggles scanning cheat files for all CRCs of the game. With this enabled available cheats for the game serial with different CRCs will also be loaded.

rows.heading: CHEATS
rows.label: Download Cheats
rows.desc: Downloads cheats for this game from the cheat collections on GitHub.

rows.heading: CHEATS
rows.label: Enter Cheat Code
rows.desc: Adds a raw cheat code: a name first, then one code line at a time. Encrypted codes are not supported.

rows.heading: PATCHES
rows.label: Show Patches For All CRCs
rows.code_label: Those of other versions of the game too
rows.desc: Toggles scanning patch files for all CRCs of the game. With this enabled available patches for the game serial with different CRCs will also be loaded.

rows.heading: QUICK SETUP
rows.label: Fastest
rows.desc: Renders at the PS2's native resolution with no extra processing. For games that are slow at any setting.

rows.heading: QUICK SETUP
rows.label: Balanced
rows.desc: Renders at about 1080p with slightly sharper textures. Suits most games.

rows.heading: QUICK SETUP
rows.label: Sharpest
rows.desc: Renders at about 1440p and upscales to 4K with AMD FSR 1, with the sharpest textures. For games with performance to spare.

rows.heading: QUICK SETUP
rows.label: Automatic Quality
rows.desc: Lowers the internal resolution when the game cannot hold full speed, and raises it again when there is headroom. Does not help when the CPU is the bottleneck.

rows.heading: QUICK SETUP
rows.label: Free Unused Targets When Memory Is Short
rows.desc: At very high resolutions, or with a texture pack, a heavy game can fill the console's graphics memory, and draws then go without their textures. Frees render targets that haven't been drawn to for two frames and whose picture is kept elsewhere, as is done after 60 frames anyway, when that happens or when targets hold more than 6 GB; when it happens, also the cached textures no draw uses (replacements are loaded again when needed). The resolution stays as you chose.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Graphics API
rows.desc: Selects the API used to render the emulated GS.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: paraLLEl-GS Samples
rows.desc: Determines how many samples paraLLEl-GS takes per pixel. More samples give a smoother, sharper picture. Higher values reduce performance.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: paraLLEl-GS Double Resolution
rows.desc: Renders at twice the PS2's resolution when using 4 or more samples. Sharper, but reduces performance.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: paraLLEl-GS Sharp 2D
rows.desc: Applies super-sampling to text, menus and other 2D elements. Sharper, but may cause seams in some games.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: paraLLEl-GS Early Submit
rows.code_label: paraLLEl-GS hands work over as it goes (experimental)
rows.desc: Submits work to the GPU while the frame is still being recorded. Can help games that read back the screen. May cause issues in some games.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: paraLLEl-GS Full-Detail Effects
rows.desc: Keeps full detail in effects that render to a texture, such as blur, glow and depth of field. Reduces performance.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: paraLLEl-GS Shared Frames
rows.code_label: paraLLEl-GS pictures shared with the graphics device (experimental)
rows.desc: Passes paraLLEl-GS frames to the display without copying them on the CPU. May cause issues in some games.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Aspect Ratio
rows.desc: Selects the aspect ratio to display the game content at.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: FMV Aspect Ratio Override
rows.desc: Selects the aspect ratio for display when a FMV is detected as playing.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Pillarbox Fill
rows.desc: Selects what fills the sides of the screen when the game is 4:3. Dark gray wears an OLED screen more evenly than black.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Deinterlacing
rows.desc:
Determines the deinterlacing method to be used on the interlaced screen of the emulated console.
Automatic should be able to correctly deinterlace most games, but if you see visibly shaky graphics, try one of the other options.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Bilinear Filtering
rows.desc: Smooths out the image when upscaling the console to the screen.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Apply Widescreen Patches
rows.desc: Automatically loads and applies widescreen patches on game start. Can cause issues.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Apply No-Interlacing Patches
rows.desc: Automatically loads and applies no-interlacing patches on game start. Can cause issues.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Widescreen Patch
rows.desc: Applies this game's widescreen patch, if one exists.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: No-Interlacing Patch
rows.desc: Applies this game's no-interlacing patch, if one exists.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Anti-Blur
rows.desc: Enables internal Anti-Blur hacks. Less accurate than PS2 rendering but will make a lot of games look less blurry.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Integer Scaling
rows.desc: Adds padding to the display area to ensure that the ratio between pixels on the host to pixels in the console is an integer number. May result in a sharper image in some 2D games.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Screen Offsets
rows.desc: Enables PCRTC Offsets which position the screen as the game requests.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Show Overscan
rows.desc: Enables the option to show the overscan area on games which draw more than the safe area of the screen.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Disable Interlace Offset
rows.desc: Disables interlacing offset which may reduce blurring in some situations.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Vertical Stretch
rows.desc: Increases or decreases the virtual picture size vertically.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Crop Left
rows.desc: Changes the number of pixels cropped from the left side of the display.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Crop Top
rows.desc: Changes the number of pixels cropped from the top of the display.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Crop Right
rows.desc: Changes the number of pixels cropped from the right side of the display.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Crop Bottom
rows.desc: Changes the number of pixels cropped from the bottom of the display.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Output Resolution
rows.desc: Selects the resolution sent to the TV. A lower resolution on a 1080p or 1440p TV saves GPU time.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: HDR
rows.desc: Sends the picture to the TV as HDR10, with the game's brightest parts brighter. Requires HDR enabled in the console's settings and a TV that supports HDR; otherwise the picture stays SDR.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: HDR Peak Brightness
rows.desc: Sets how bright the game's brightest parts (the sky, lights, fire) become in HDR. Set it near the TV's peak brightness. Off shows the SDR picture as it is, at the white level.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: HDR White Level
rows.desc: Sets how bright white is in HDR, for the menus and the game's ordinary whites. 203 nits is the HDR reference; raise it if the picture looks dim.

rows.heading: DISPLAY
rows.label: Calibrate HDR
rows.desc: Shows a test screen: raising the X in a square until it vanishes sets the peak brightness, then a gray scale sets the white level.

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: Internal Resolution
rows.desc: Multiplies the render resolution by the specified factor (upscaling).

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: Upscaling and Sharpening
rows.desc: Selects how the image is upscaled and sharpened. FSR 1 renders at a lower resolution and upscales with AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution; NIS upscales and sharpens with NVIDIA Image Scaling; Sharpen uses FidelityFX Contrast Adaptive Sharpening.

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: Sharpness
rows.desc: Determines the intensity the sharpening effect in CAS post-processing.

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: Texture Filtering
rows.desc: Selects where bilinear filtering is utilized when rendering textures.

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: Trilinear Filtering
rows.desc: Selects where trilinear filtering is utilized when rendering textures.

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: Anisotropic Filtering
rows.desc: Reduces texture aliasing at extreme viewing angles.

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: Dithering
rows.desc: Selects the type of dithering applies when the game requests it.

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: Blending Accuracy
rows.desc: Determines the level of accuracy when emulating blend modes not supported by the host graphics API.

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: Mipmapping
rows.desc: Enables mipmapping, which some games require to render correctly. Mipmapping uses progressively lower resolution variants of textures at progressively further distances to reduce processing load and avoid visual artifacts.

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: Accurate Alpha Test
rows.desc: Enables accurate alpha testing, which some games require to render correctly. This may require more draw calls and result in a speed penalty.

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: AA1
rows.desc: Enables AA1 (PS2 antialiasing), which some games require to render correctly. This may result in a heavy performance penalty.

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: Rasterizer Ordered View
rows.desc: Enables Rasterizer Ordered View (ROV), which allows feedback loops to be executed with fewer draw calls. Can improve performance in feedback heavy games with higher accuracy settings.

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: Software Rendering Threads
rows.desc: Number of threads to use in addition to the main GS thread for rasterization.

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: Auto Flush
rows.desc: Force a primitive flush when a framebuffer is also an input texture.

rows.heading: RENDERING
rows.label: Mipmapping
rows.desc: Enables mipmapping, which some games require to render correctly. Mipmapping uses progressively lower resolution variants of textures at progressively further distances to reduce processing load and avoid visual artifacts.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Manual Hardware Renderer Fixes
rows.desc: Disables automatic hardware fixes, allowing you to set fixes manually.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: CPU Sprite Render Size
rows.desc: The maximum target memory width that will allow the CPU Sprite Renderer to activate on.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: CPU Sprite Render Level
rows.desc: Determines filter level for CPU sprite render.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Software CLUT Render
rows.desc: Tries to detect when a game is drawing its own color palette and then renders it in software, instead of on the GPU.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: GPU Target CLUT
rows.desc: Tries to detect when a game is drawing its own color palette and then renders it on the GPU with special handling.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Skip Draw Range Start
rows.desc: Completely skips drawing surfaces from the starting index up to the ending index.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Skip Draw Range End
rows.desc: Completely skips drawing surfaces from the starting index up to the ending index.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Auto Flush
rows.desc: Forces a primitive flush when a framebuffer is also an input texture. Fixes some processing effects such as the shadows in the Jak series and radiosity in GTA:SA.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Framebuffer Conversion
rows.desc: Convert 4-bit and 8-bit framebuffer on the CPU instead of the GPU.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Disable Depth Conversion
rows.desc: Disable the support of depth buffers in the texture cache.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Disable Safe Features
rows.desc: This option disables multiple safe features.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Disable Render Fixes
rows.desc: This option disables game-specific render fixes.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Preload Frame Data
rows.desc: Uploads GS data when rendering a new frame to reproduce some effects accurately.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Disable Partial Source Invalidation
rows.desc: Removes texture cache entries when there is any intersection, rather than only the intersected areas.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Texture Inside RT
rows.desc: Allows the texture cache to reuse as an input texture the inner portion of a previous framebuffer.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Read Targets When Closing
rows.desc: Flushes all targets in the texture cache back to local memory when shutting down.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Estimate Texture Region
rows.desc: Attempts to reduce the texture size when games do not set it themselves (e.g. Snowblind games).

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Draw Buffering
rows.desc: Attempts to reduce draw calls in games which do heavy context switching for blending purposes.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Rewrite Large ST
rows.desc: Rewrite large ST coordinates and clamp the values.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Target Page Rearranging
rows.desc: Rearranges memory pages of a target if the game changes the layout at that current VRAM address.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: GPU Palette Conversion
rows.code_label: Palette conversion on the graphics chip
rows.desc: When enabled GPU converts colormap-textures, otherwise the CPU will. It is a trade-off between GPU and CPU.

rows.heading: HARDWARE FIXES
rows.label: Limit Depth to 24 Bits
rows.desc: Truncate 32-bit depth values to 24 bits. Helps games struggling with Z-fighting.

rows.heading: UPSCALING FIXES
rows.label: Half Pixel Offset
rows.desc: Might fix some misaligned fog, bloom, or blend effect.

choices.name: Align to Native - with Texture Offset

rows.heading: UPSCALING FIXES
rows.label: Native Scaling
rows.desc: Emulates native PS2 coordinate scaling behavior when upscaling to reduce misalignment artifacts and seams in games that draw custom 2D elements.

rows.heading: UPSCALING FIXES
rows.label: Round Sprite
rows.desc: Adjusts sprite coordinates.

rows.heading: UPSCALING FIXES
rows.label: Bilinear Dirty Upscale
rows.desc: Can smooth out textures due to be bilinear filtered when upscaling. E.g. Brave sun glare.

rows.heading: UPSCALING FIXES
rows.label: Texture Offsets X
rows.desc: Adjusts target texture offsets.

rows.heading: UPSCALING FIXES
rows.label: Texture Offsets Y
rows.desc: Adjusts target texture offsets.

rows.heading: UPSCALING FIXES
rows.label: Align Sprite
rows.desc: Fixes issues with upscaling (vertical lines) in some games.

rows.heading: UPSCALING FIXES
rows.label: Merge Sprite
rows.desc: Replaces post-processing multiple paving sprites by a single fat sprite. It reduces various upscaling lines.

rows.heading: UPSCALING FIXES
rows.label: Force Even Sprite Position
rows.desc: Lowers the GS precision to avoid gaps between pixels when upscaling. Fixes the text on Wild Arms games.

rows.heading: UPSCALING FIXES
rows.label: Unscaled Palette Texture Draws
rows.desc: Forces palette texture draws to render at native resolution.

rows.heading: TEXTURE REPLACEMENT
rows.label: Load Textures
rows.desc: Loads replacement textures where available and user-provided.

rows.heading: TEXTURE REPLACEMENT
rows.label: Asynchronous Texture Loading
rows.desc: Loads replacement textures on a worker thread, reducing microstutter when replacements are enabled.

rows.heading: TEXTURE REPLACEMENT
rows.label: Precache Textures
rows.desc: Preloads all replacement textures to memory. Not necessary with asynchronous loading.

rows.heading: TEXTURE REPLACEMENT
rows.label: HD Texture Packs
rows.desc: Opens the texture pack manager, which lists the packs on the console, USB drives and network shares by game, downloads packs from the Internet Archive one after another, and moves or deletes them. Packs can be several GB.

rows.heading: TEXTURE REPLACEMENT
rows.label: Stop Download
rows.desc: Stops the download. Files already unpacked are kept.

rows.heading: TEXTURE REPLACEMENT
rows.label: Download Connections
rows.desc: Sets how many connections a texture pack is downloaded over at once, each fetching a piece of it. More connections are faster when the Internet Archive limits each one. Applies to the next download.

rows.heading: TEXTURE REPLACEMENT
rows.label: Dump Textures
rows.desc: Dumps replaceable textures to disk. Will reduce performance.

rows.heading: TEXTURE REPLACEMENT
rows.label: Dump Mipmaps
rows.desc: Includes mipmaps when dumping textures.

rows.heading: TEXTURE REPLACEMENT
rows.label: Dump FMV Textures
rows.desc: Allows texture dumping when FMVs are active. You should not enable this.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Anti-Aliasing
rows.desc: Smooths the jagged edges of the picture. FXAA is fast but slightly soft; SMAA gives sharper edges at a small cost; SSAA scales the picture of the chosen internal resolution down to the screen, for the least shimmer when it is larger than the screen (6x and up at 4K), and disables FSR 1 while chosen; SSAA + SMAA applies both.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: SSAA Filter
rows.desc: Selects how SSAA scales the picture down to the screen. Soft averages every pixel covered, with the least shimmer. Sharp uses a Lanczos filter for crisper edges.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: TV Shader
rows.desc: Applies a shader which replicates the visual effects of different styles of television sets.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Shader Preset
rows.desc: Applies a shader preset that makes the picture look like an old TV, with CRT shaders, composite or S-Video signal effects, and film grain.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Load Custom Shader Preset
rows.desc: Loads a libretro shader preset (.slangp) from a "shaders" folder on a USB drive or in the title folder.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Debanding
rows.desc: Smooths the color bands in skies, fog and dark gradients while keeping edges and detail. Low removes the fine steps of 32-bit color; High removes the wider steps of 16-bit color.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Color Blindness Filter
rows.desc: Shifts colors that are hard to tell apart to ones that are easier to distinguish. Red-Weak and Green-Weak help with reds and greens; Blue-Weak with blues and yellows. Applies to the game's picture only.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Shade Boost
rows.desc: Enables brightness/contrast/gamma/saturation adjustment.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Brightness
rows.desc: Adjusts brightness. 50 is normal.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Contrast
rows.desc: Adjusts contrast. 50 is normal.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Gamma
rows.desc: Adjusts gamma. 50 is normal.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Saturation
rows.desc: Adjusts saturation. 50 is normal.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Frame Generation
rows.desc: Generates extra frames between the game's frames, so a 30 FPS game is shown at 60 FPS. Increases input lag slightly and can cause smearing on fast movement.

choices.name: 30 to 60 FPS, 60 to 120 FPS at 120 Hz

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Frame Generation Method
rows.desc: Selects how the extra frames are made. Default uses a motion search; AMD FSR 3 Optical Flow handles small, fast movement better and keeps static elements such as a score or a map still; MihawkGen uses a small trained network that looks only at the two frames and leaves unmoving parts as they were.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Optical Flow Quality
rows.desc: Determines the quality of the AMD FSR 3 optical flow. Higher quality reduces performance.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Disable Frame Generation During FMVs
rows.desc: Disables frame generation while the game plays an FMV.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Steady 30 FPS
rows.desc: Limits the game's frames to every second vsync, so a game that varies between 30 and 60 FPS is shown at an even 30 FPS that frame generation doubles to 60 FPS (120 FPS at 120 Hz). For games that cannot hold 60 FPS.

rows.heading: POST-PROCESSING
rows.label: Show Frame Generation Motion
rows.desc: Shows, in the generated frames, what AMD FSR 3 optical flow decided for each pixel instead of the picture: red for both frames, green for the newer only, blue for the older only, gray for a mix. For debugging only.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Uncompressed Feedback Targets
rows.desc: Keeps render targets uncompressed when glow and flare effects read them. Can improve performance in some games, but may cause issues in others.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Disable Render Target Compression
rows.desc: Creates render targets without color compression. Can improve or reduce performance depending on the game, and may cause issues.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Skip Redundant Barriers
rows.code_label: Leave out barriers with nothing to wait for
rows.desc: Skips GPU waits when nothing has been drawn since the last one. Disable it if effects look wrong.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: GS Thread Split
rows.desc: Splits the GS thread in two: one reads the game's graphics commands, the other draws. Can improve performance in games limited by the GS thread. Check does the same work on one thread, to compare the picture.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Reuse Render Target Copies
rows.desc: Reuses copies of the screen for glow and blur effects when nothing has changed. Disable it if an effect looks a frame behind.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Shared Render Target Memory
rows.desc: Allocates render targets from shared memory blocks instead of one allocation each. Reduces the time spent creating textures at high internal resolutions.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Keep ROV Render Passes
rows.code_label: Keep the ordered view's render passes
rows.desc: Keeps draws that use the Rasterizer Ordered View in the same render pass. Greatly reduces CPU work in scenes with many lights.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Hardware Download Mode
rows.desc: Changes synchronization behavior for GS downloads.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Texture Preloading
rows.desc: Uploads full textures to the GPU on use, rather than only the utilized regions. Can improve performance in some games.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Extended Upscaling Multipliers
rows.desc: Displays additional, very high upscaling multipliers dependent on GPU and driver capability.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Internal Resolution
rows.desc: Multiplies the render resolution by the specified factor (upscaling).

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Override Texture Barriers
rows.desc: Forces texture barrier functionality to the specified value.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: ROV Barriers Vulkan
rows.code_label: Extra barriers with the ordered view
rows.desc: Forces extra barriers when using ROV with Vulkan to fix graphical issues present in some games and hardware configurations.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Disable Shader Cache
rows.desc: Prevents the loading and saving of shaders/pipelines to disk.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Disable Vertex Shader Expand
rows.desc: Falls back to the CPU for expanding sprites/lines.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Spin CPU During Readbacks
rows.desc: Does useless work on the CPU during readbacks to prevent it from going into powersave modes. May improve performance during readbacks but with a significant increase in power usage.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Spin GPU During Readbacks
rows.desc: Submits useless work to the GPU during readbacks to prevent it from going into powersave modes. May improve performance during readbacks but with a significant increase in power usage.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Disable Framebuffer Fetch
rows.desc: Prevents the usage of framebuffer fetch when supported by host GPU.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: Use Blit Swap Chain
rows.desc: Uses a blit presentation model instead of flipping when using the Direct3D 11 graphics API. This usually results in slower performance, but may be required for some streaming applications, or to uncap framerates on some systems.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: NTSC Frame Rate
rows.desc: Sets the frame rate used for NTSC games.

rows.heading: ADVANCED
rows.label: PAL Frame Rate
rows.desc: Sets the frame rate used for PAL games.

rows.heading: ON-SCREEN DISPLAY
rows.label: OSD Scale
rows.desc: Scales the size of the onscreen OSD from 50% to 500%.

rows.heading: ON-SCREEN DISPLAY
rows.label: OSD Margin
rows.desc: Sets the distance in pixels from the edges of the screen for OSD elements.

rows.heading: ON-SCREEN DISPLAY
rows.label: OSD Messages Position
rows.desc: Determines where on-screen display messages are positioned.

rows.heading: ON-SCREEN DISPLAY
rows.label: OSD Performance Position
rows.desc: Position of a variety of on-screen performance data points as selected by the user.

rows.heading: ON-SCREEN DISPLAY
rows.label: Bold OSD Text
rows.desc: Draws OSD text with heavier weight for improved readability.

rows.heading: ON-SCREEN DISPLAY
rows.label: Move OSD Periodically
rows.code_label: Move the figures from corner to corner
rows.desc: Moves the on-screen display to another corner every five minutes to prevent burn-in.

rows.heading: ON-SCREEN DISPLAY
rows.label: OSD Style
rows.desc: Selects how performance data is shown. Panel shows one panel with sections and a frame time graph; Lines shows PCSX2's lines of text.

rows.heading: ON-SCREEN DISPLAY
rows.label: Performance Overlay Size
rows.desc: Selects how much of the performance overlay is shown. Minimal shows the FPS; Compact adds GPU and CPU usage; Full adds frame times, a frame time graph, the internal resolution and hardware info. Custom shows the items enabled under Show.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: Show Speed Percentages
rows.desc: Shows the current emulation speed of the system as a percentage.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: Show FPS
rows.desc: Shows the number of internal video frames displayed per second by the system.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: Show VPS
rows.desc: Shows the number of Vsyncs performed per second by the system.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: Show Resolution
rows.desc: Shows the internal resolution of the game.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: Show CPU Usage
rows.desc: Shows the host's CPU utilization based on threads.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: Show GPU Usage
rows.desc: Shows the host's GPU utilization.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: Show Frame Times
rows.desc: Displays a graph showing the average frametimes.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: Show Hardware Info
rows.desc: Shows the current system CPU and GPU information.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: Show GS Statistics
rows.desc: Shows statistics about the emulated GS such as primitives and draw calls.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: Show GPU Pipeline Statistics
rows.desc: Shows GPU vertex shader and pixels shader invocations.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: Show Status Indicators
rows.desc: Shows icon indicators for emulation states such as Pausing, Turbo, Fast-Forward, and Slow-Motion.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: Show Settings
rows.desc: Displays various settings and the current values of those settings in the bottom-right corner of the display.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: Show Patches
rows.desc: Shows the amount of currently active patches/cheats in the bottom-right corner of the display.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: Show Inputs
rows.desc: Shows the current controller state of the system in the bottom-left corner of the display.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: Show Texture Replacement Status
rows.desc: Shows the status of the number of dumped and loaded texture replacements in the top-right corner of the display.

rows.heading: SHOW
rows.label: Show Version
rows.desc: Shows the current version in the on-screen display.

rows.heading: CONFIGURATION
rows.label: Synchronization
rows.desc:
When the emulation isn't running at 100% speed, adjusts the tempo of the audio
which produces much nicer sound during fast-forward/slowdown.

rows.heading: CONFIGURATION
rows.label: Expansion Mode
rows.desc: Determines how audio is expanded from stereo to surround for supported games.

rows.heading: CONFIGURATION
rows.label: Buffer Size
rows.desc: Determines the amount of audio buffered before being pulled by the host API.

rows.heading: CONFIGURATION
rows.label: Output Latency
rows.desc: Determines how much audio is sent to the console at once. Lower values reduce latency; raise it if the sound crackles.

rows.heading: CONTROLS
rows.label: Standard Volume
rows.desc: Controls the volume of the audio played on the host at normal speed.

rows.heading: CONTROLS
rows.label: Fast Forward Volume
rows.desc: Controls the volume of the audio played on the host when fast forwarding.

rows.heading: CONTROLS
rows.label: Mute All Sound
rows.desc: Prevents the emulator from producing any audible sound.

rows.heading: TIME STRETCH SETTINGS
rows.label: Sequence Length
rows.desc: Sets the length of the audio sequences the time stretcher processes.

rows.heading: TIME STRETCH SETTINGS
rows.label: Seekwindow Size
rows.desc: Sets the length of the window in which the time stretcher searches for the best point to join two sequences.

rows.heading: TIME STRETCH SETTINGS
rows.label: Overlap
rows.desc: Sets how long consecutive sequences overlap when the time stretcher joins them.

rows.heading: TIME STRETCH SETTINGS
rows.label: Use Quickseek
rows.desc: Uses a faster but less precise search when the time stretcher joins sequences.

rows.heading: TIME STRETCH SETTINGS
rows.label: Use Anti-Aliasing Filter
rows.desc: Applies an anti-aliasing filter when the time stretcher changes the audio's rate.

rows.heading: EXPANSION SETTINGS
rows.label: Block Size
rows.desc: Sets the size of the blocks the channel expander processes. Larger blocks increase latency.

rows.heading: EXPANSION SETTINGS
rows.label: Circular Wrap
rows.desc: Sets the angle, in degrees, over which the stereo image is spread around the listener.

rows.heading: EXPANSION SETTINGS
rows.label: Shift
rows.desc: Moves the sound field forward or backward.

rows.heading: EXPANSION SETTINGS
rows.label: Depth
rows.desc: Sets how far the sound field extends to the rear.

rows.heading: EXPANSION SETTINGS
rows.label: Focus
rows.desc: Makes the position of each sound sharper or wider.

rows.heading: EXPANSION SETTINGS
rows.label: Center Image
rows.desc: Sets how much of the sound is sent to the center channel.

rows.heading: EXPANSION SETTINGS
rows.label: Front Separation
rows.desc: Sets the stereo separation of the front channels.

rows.heading: EXPANSION SETTINGS
rows.label: Rear Separation
rows.desc: Sets the stereo separation of the rear channels.

rows.heading: EXPANSION SETTINGS
rows.label: Low Cutoff
rows.desc: Sets the lower end of the LFE channel's transition band.

rows.heading: EXPANSION SETTINGS
rows.label: High Cutoff
rows.desc: Sets the upper end of the LFE channel's transition band.

rows.heading: A MEMORY CARD FOR EACH GAME
rows.label: A MEMORY CARD FOR EACH GAME

rows.heading: A MEMORY CARD FOR EACH GAME
rows.label: This Game's Memory Card

rows.heading: CARD MANAGER
rows.label: Memory Card Manager
rows.desc: Opens the memory card manager, which copies, deletes, imports and exports saves, and creates, formats and renames memory cards.

rows.heading: SLOT 1
rows.label: Memory Card Enabled
rows.desc: If not set, this card will be considered unplugged.

rows.heading: SLOT 1
rows.label: Card Name
rows.desc: The selected memory card image will be used for this slot.

rows.heading: SLOT 2
rows.label: Memory Card Enabled
rows.desc: If not set, this card will be considered unplugged.

rows.heading: SLOT 2
rows.label: Card Name
rows.desc: The selected memory card image will be used for this slot.

rows.heading: OPTIONS
rows.label: Memory Card per Game
rows.code_label: A memory card for each game
rows.desc: Gives every game its own memory card in slot 1, created when the game first starts.

rows.heading: OPTIONS
rows.label: Folder Memory Card Filter
rows.code_label: A folder card shows only the running game's saves
rows.desc: Simulates a larger memory card by filtering saves only to the current game.

rows.heading: MEMORY CARDS AND SAVED STATES
rows.label: Backup Location
rows.desc: Selects where backups are saved. A network share must allow writing.

rows.heading: MEMORY CARDS AND SAVED STATES
rows.label: Back Up Save States
rows.desc: Includes save states in backups. When disabled, only memory cards are backed up, which is much faster.

rows.heading: MEMORY CARDS AND SAVED STATES
rows.label: Back Up Memory Cards on Close
rows.code_label: Back up the memory cards when a game is closed
rows.desc: Backs up the memory cards that changed when a game is closed. The 10 newest automatic backups are kept.

rows.heading: MEMORY CARDS AND SAVED STATES
rows.label: Replace Previous Backup
rows.code_label: Each backup replaces the one before it
rows.desc: Deletes older backups when a new one is made, so the backup folder does not fill up.

rows.heading: MEMORY CARDS AND SAVED STATES
rows.label: Back Up Now
rows.desc: Backs up all memory cards and save states.

rows.heading: MEMORY CARDS IN SYNC
rows.label: Sync Memory Cards
rows.code_label: Keep the memory cards in sync
rows.desc: Keeps memory cards in sync with the backup location on startup and after each game. When a card changed on both sides, the newer one is kept and the other is set aside. PCSX2 on PC and ARMSX2 on Android can use the same folder.

rows.heading: MEMORY CARDS IN SYNC
rows.label: Sync Memory Cards Now
rows.desc: Syncs the memory cards with the backup location.

rows.heading: BACKUPS ON USB DRIVE 1
rows.label: Refresh
rows.desc: Refreshes the list of backups.

rows.heading: NETWORK ADAPTER
rows.label: Enable Network Adapter
rows.desc: Enables the network adapter for online functionality and LAN play.

rows.heading: NETWORK ADAPTER
rows.label: DNS1 Mode
rows.desc: Determines how primary DNS requests are handled.

rows.heading: NETWORK ADAPTER
rows.label: DNS1 Address
rows.desc: Sets the DNS server games use to find their online servers. Revival services such as PS2 Online and PS Rewired keep many games online; their websites list the games they support.

rows.heading: NETWORK ADAPTER
rows.label: DNS2 Mode
rows.desc: Determines how secondary DNS requests are handled.

rows.heading: NETWORK ADAPTER
rows.label: DNS2 Address
rows.desc: Sets the address of the secondary DNS server, one number at a time.

rows.heading: NETWORK ADAPTER
rows.label: Test DNS
rows.desc: Asks the DNS servers set above for the service's website (three tries) and reports whether they answer and how fast. The console's own DNS server is tested in the console's settings.

rows.heading: HARD DRIVE
rows.label: Enable HDD
rows.desc: Enables the internal Hard Disk Drive for expanded storage.

rows.heading: HARD DRIVE
rows.label: Create 40 GB HDD Image
rows.code_label: Make a new hard drive of 40 GB
rows.desc: Creates an empty 40 GB HDD image, the size of the official drive. The game, or the software that came with the drive, formats it.

rows.heading: HARD DRIVE
rows.label: Create 120 GB HDD Image
rows.code_label: Make a new hard drive of 120 GB
rows.desc: Creates an empty 120 GB HDD image, for more than a few games. The file only takes space as it is written to.

rows.heading: A PHONE OR A COMPUTER
rows.label: Remote Control Page
rows.desc: Opens a web page (port 3311) for starting games, managing save states and typing text from a phone or computer.

rows.heading: A PHONE OR A COMPUTER
rows.label: Show QR Code
rows.desc: Shows the page's address as a QR code to scan with a phone.

rows.heading: A PHONE OR A COMPUTER
rows.label: Generate New Key
rows.desc: Creates a new key for the page. The old address stops working.

rows.heading: RETROACHIEVEMENTS
rows.label: Logout
rows.desc: Logs out of RetroAchievements.

rows.heading: RETROACHIEVEMENTS
rows.label: Login
rows.desc: Logs in to RetroAchievements.

rows.heading: RETROACHIEVEMENTS
rows.label: Enable Achievements
rows.desc: When enabled and logged in, PCSX2 will scan for achievements on startup.

rows.heading: WHILE PLAYING
rows.label: Show Achievement Notifications
rows.code_label: Say when an achievement is earned
rows.desc: Displays popup messages on events such as achievement unlocks and game completion.

rows.heading: WHILE PLAYING
rows.label: Use System Trophy Notifications
rows.desc: Announces unlocked achievements as the console's trophy notifications, with the badge and the trophy sound, and the platinum trophy's notification when every achievement of a game is unlocked. When disabled, PCSX2's silent notifications are shown over the game.

rows.heading: WHILE PLAYING
rows.label: Show Leaderboard Notifications
rows.code_label: Say when a leaderboard attempt starts and ends
rows.desc: Displays popup messages when starting, submitting, or failing a leaderboard challenge.

rows.heading: WHILE PLAYING
rows.label: Enable In-Game Overlays
rows.desc: Shows icons in the screen when a challenge/primed achievement is active.

rows.heading: WHILE PLAYING
rows.label: Enable In-Game Leaderboard Overlays
rows.code_label: Show a leaderboard's time or score as it runs
rows.desc: Shows icons in the screen when leaderboard tracking is active.

rows.heading: WHILE PLAYING
rows.label: Unlock Notification Duration
rows.desc: Determines the display duration for achievement unlock popups.

rows.heading: WHILE PLAYING
rows.label: Leaderboard Notification Duration
rows.code_label: How long a leaderboard's notice stays
rows.desc: Determines the display duration for leaderboard notification popups.

rows.heading: WHILE PLAYING
rows.label: Notification Position
rows.desc: Determines where achievement/leaderboard notification popups are positioned on the screen.

rows.heading: WHILE PLAYING
rows.label: Overlay Position
rows.code_label: Where the small pictures are shown
rows.desc: Determines where achievement/leaderboard overlays are positioned on the screen.

rows.heading: MORE
rows.label: Enable Encore Mode
rows.desc: When enabled, each session will behave as if no achievements have been unlocked.

rows.heading: MORE
rows.label: Enable Spectator Mode
rows.desc: When enabled, PCSX2 will assume all achievements are locked and not send any unlock notifications to the server.

rows.heading: MORE
rows.label: Test Unofficial Achievements
rows.desc: When enabled, PCSX2 will list achievements from unofficial sets. Please note that these achievements are not tracked by RetroAchievements, so they unlock every time.

rows.heading: SOUND EFFECTS
rows.label: Enable Sound Effects
rows.desc: Plays sound effects for events such as achievement unlocks and leaderboard submissions.

rows.heading: SOUND EFFECTS
rows.label: Unlock Sound
rows.desc: Plays a sound effect when an achievement is unlocked.

rows.heading: SOUND EFFECTS
rows.label: Leaderboard Sound
rows.desc: Plays a sound effect when submitting a leaderboard entry.

rows.heading: SOUND EFFECTS
rows.label: Notification Sound
rows.desc: Plays a sound effect when achievement notifications appear.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PROFILES
rows.label: Input Profile
rows.desc: The selected input profile will be used for this game.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PROFILES
rows.label: Save Profile
rows.code_label: Save the controls as a profile...
rows.desc: Stores the current settings to an input profile.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PROFILES
rows.label: Load Profile
rows.code_label: Load a profile into the controls...
rows.desc: Replaces these settings with a previously saved input profile.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PROFILES
rows.label: Save Swapped Profile
rows.code_label: Make a profile with Cross and Circle swapped
rows.desc: Saves an input profile with Cross and Circle swapped, for Japanese games.

rows.heading: ALL PORTS
rows.label: Reset Bindings
rows.code_label: Put the buttons back as they were
rows.desc: Resets all controller ports and hotkeys to their default bindings.

rows.heading: SINGSTAR
rows.label: USB Microphones
rows.desc: Uses the controller's microphone or a headset as the PS2's USB microphones, for SingStar and other singing games.

rows.heading: SINGSTAR
rows.label: Test Player 1 Microphone
rows.desc: Records five seconds of speech or song and plays it back as a game would hear it; the boot log's "mic test" lines report how the microphone performed. Only available when no game is running.

rows.heading: SINGSTAR
rows.label: Test Player 2 Microphone
rows.desc: Records five seconds of speech or song and plays it back as a game would hear it; the boot log's "mic test" lines report how the microphone performed. Only available when no game is running.

rows.heading: LIGHT GUN
rows.label: Light Gun (GunCon 2)
rows.desc: Connects a GunCon 2 to the PS2's USB port 1, or two GunCon 2s to ports 1 and 2 for two players, for light gun games. Best set in a game's own settings: a game that does not expect a light gun may not see its controller. Two guns use USB port 2, which the USB microphones also use.

rows.heading: PLAYERS
rows.label: One or Two Players
rows.desc: Puts player 1 on port 1 and player 2 on port 2, without a multitap.

rows.heading: PLAYERS
rows.label: Four Players, Multitap on Port 1
rows.code_label: Up to four players, multitap in port 1
rows.desc: Puts players 1 to 4 on a multitap in port 1, for most games with three or four players.

rows.heading: PLAYERS
rows.label: Four Players, Multitap on Port 2
rows.code_label: Up to four players, multitap in port 2
rows.desc: Puts player 1 on port 1 and players 2 to 4 on a multitap in port 2, for games that need it there.

rows.heading: PLAYERS
rows.label: Player Color Light Bar
rows.code_label: Light bar in the player's colour
rows.desc: Sets each controller's light bar to its player's color: blue, red, green, pink.

rows.heading: BY HAND
rows.label: Multitap on Console Port 1
rows.desc: Enables an additional three controller slots. Not supported in all games.

rows.heading: BY HAND
rows.label: Multitap on Console Port 2
rows.desc: Enables an additional three controller slots. Not supported in all games.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PORT 1
rows.label: Controller
rows.desc: Selects the controller connected to this port.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PORT 1
rows.label: Map to Console Controller
rows.code_label: Map it to a controller of the console
rows.desc: Maps every button of this port to the console's controller 1, or the first controller when there are fewer.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PORT 1
rows.label: Map to USB Controller
rows.code_label: Map it to a USB controller
rows.desc: Maps this port to a controller connected to the console's USB port.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PORT 1
rows.label: Large (Low Frequency) Motor
rows.desc: Selects the motor that plays the game's low frequency vibration.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PORT 1
rows.label: Small (High Frequency) Motor
rows.desc: Selects the motor that plays the game's high frequency vibration.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PORT 1
rows.label: Invert Left Stick
rows.desc: Inverts the direction of the left analog stick.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PORT 1
rows.label: Invert Right Stick
rows.desc: Inverts the direction of the right analog stick.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PORT 1
rows.label: Analog Deadzone
rows.desc: Sets the analog stick deadzone, i.e. the fraction of the stick movement which will be ignored.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PORT 1
rows.label: Analog Sensitivity
rows.desc: Sets the analog stick axis scaling factor. Modern controllers with square pickup zones, e.g. DualShock 4, Xbox One have better diagonal inputs at a range between 130-140%, but this will cause axes to reach max input early.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PORT 1
rows.label: Use Diagonal Scale Correction
rows.desc: Transforms analog stick pickup zone from a square to a circle, allows for full input at diagonals without also scaling the X and Y axes. Ideal for modern controllers with square pickup zones, e.g. DualShock 4, Xbox One. Setting Analog Sensitivity to 100% is recommended with this setting.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PORT 1
rows.label: Large Motor Vibration Scale
rows.desc: Increases or decreases the intensity of low frequency vibration sent by the game.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PORT 1
rows.label: Small Motor Vibration Scale
rows.desc: Increases or decreases the intensity of high frequency vibration sent by the game.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PORT 1
rows.label: Button/Trigger Deadzone
rows.desc: Sets the deadzone for activating buttons/triggers, i.e. the fraction of the trigger which will be ignored.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PORT 1
rows.label: Pressure Modifier Amount
rows.desc: Sets the pressure when the modifier button is held.

rows.heading: CONTROLLER PORT 2
rows.label: Controller
rows.desc: Selects the controller connected to this port.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: Close Game Combination
rows.desc: Selects the buttons that close the game when held.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: Close Game Hold Time
rows.desc: Determines how long the buttons must be held to close the game.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: Pressure from R2
rows.desc: Uses how far R2 is pulled as the pressure of the face buttons and D-pad, for games with pressure-sensitive buttons.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: Left Stick Response
rows.desc: Determines how the stick responds. Linear follows the stick as pushed; Gentle to Gentlest move less for a small push, for finer control near the center, while a full push still reaches the maximum.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: Right Stick Response
rows.desc: Determines how the stick responds. Linear follows the stick as pushed; Gentle to Gentlest move less for a small push, for finer control near the center, while a full push still reaches the maximum.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: Motion Aiming
rows.desc: Aims the GunCon 2 light gun by moving the controller while a GunCon 2 is connected. Hold R3 briefly to recenter; hold it for two seconds to calibrate the screen.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: Aiming Mode
rows.desc: Selects how motion aiming follows the controller. Absolute aims where the controller points, without drift. Relative adds up the controller's turns like a mouse and stops at the edges.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: Aiming Range
rows.desc: Determines how far the controller must turn to aim at the edge of the screen with absolute aiming. Calibrated uses the screen as measured by pointing at its corners.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: Calibrate Screen
rows.desc: Calibrates the screen for motion aiming: back in the game, point at the top-left corner and press R3, then at the bottom-right corner and press R3. Holding R3 for two seconds during a game does the same.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: Aiming Smoothing
rows.desc: Steadies a still hand without slowing a quick sweep, with absolute aiming.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: Controller Grip
rows.desc: Selects how the controller is held for absolute aiming: in both hands, or upright in one hand with the index finger on R2 like a pistol. Automatic detects it from how the controller is held when the aim is recentered.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: Light Gun Trigger Feel
rows.code_label: R2's click for the light gun
rows.desc: Makes R2 resist and then give way like a trigger while a GunCon 2 is connected, firing the shot with the click.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: Relative Aiming Range
rows.code_label: Aim like a mouse: how far to turn to the edge
rows.desc: Determines how far the controller must turn to aim at the edge of the screen with relative aiming.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: PlayStation Move Aiming
rows.code_label: Aim with a PlayStation Move (Move Management)
rows.desc: Aims player 1's GunCon 2 with a PlayStation Move, with a Navigation controller as its D-pad. Requires the Move Management payload. Press Select on the Move to recenter.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: USB Keyboard
rows.desc: Allows a USB keyboard to type in the menus and to act as a PS2 keyboard in games that support one.

rows.heading: THE CONSOLE'S CONTROLLERS
rows.label: USB Controllers
rows.desc: Allows controllers connected to the console's USB ports to be used, such as a DualShock 3, Xbox 360 controllers, guitars and drums. May not work with every controller.

rows.heading: EMOTIONENGINE (MIPS-IV)
rows.label: Rounding Mode
rows.desc: Determines how the results of floating-point operations are rounded. Some games need specific settings.

rows.heading: EMOTIONENGINE (MIPS-IV)
rows.label: Division Rounding Mode
rows.desc: Determines how the results of floating-point division is rounded. Some games need specific settings.

rows.heading: EMOTIONENGINE (MIPS-IV)
rows.label: Clamping Mode
rows.desc: Determines how out-of-range floating point numbers are handled. Some games need specific settings.

rows.heading: EMOTIONENGINE (MIPS-IV)
rows.label: Enable Recompiler
rows.desc: Performs just-in-time binary translation of 64-bit MIPS-IV machine code to native code.

rows.heading: EMOTIONENGINE (MIPS-IV)
rows.label: Enable Cache (Slow)
rows.desc: Enables emulation of the EE's hardware cache. Interpreter only, provided for diagnostics.

rows.heading: EMOTIONENGINE (MIPS-IV)
rows.label: INTC Spin Detection
rows.desc: Huge speedup for some games, with almost no compatibility side effects.

rows.heading: EMOTIONENGINE (MIPS-IV)
rows.label: Wait Loop Detection
rows.desc: Moderate speedup for some games, with no known side effects.

rows.heading: EMOTIONENGINE (MIPS-IV)
rows.label: Wait Loop Detection Across Two Blocks
rows.desc: Also skips wait loops the game splits in two: a test of a value in memory, then a read of it that jumps back to the test. Time spent spinning goes to the next event at once, as wait loop detection does for the one-block kind. Not yet tested on a console: a game that hangs or misbehaves with it on needs it off.

rows.heading: EMOTIONENGINE (MIPS-IV)
rows.label: Enable Fast Memory Access
rows.desc: Uses backpatching to avoid register flushing on every memory access.

rows.heading: EMOTIONENGINE (MIPS-IV)
rows.label: Pause On TLB Miss
rows.desc: Pauses the virtual machine when a TLB miss occurs, instead of ignoring it and continuing.

rows.heading: EMOTIONENGINE (MIPS-IV)
rows.label: IOP Stores Inline
rows.desc: The IOP recompiler writes stores to IOP memory itself instead of calling the memory handlers. Not yet tested on a console: a game that hangs or loses sound with it on needs it off.

rows.heading: EMOTIONENGINE (MIPS-IV)
rows.label: Enable Extended RAM (Dev Console)
rows.desc: Exposes additional memory to the virtual machine, expanding the EE and IOP memory to 128MB and 8MB respectively.

rows.heading: VECTOR UNITS (VU)
rows.label: VU0 Rounding Mode
rows.desc: Determines how the results of floating-point operations are rounded. Some games need specific settings.

rows.heading: VECTOR UNITS (VU)
rows.label: VU0 Clamping Mode
rows.desc: Determines how out-of-range floating point numbers are handled. Some games need specific settings.

rows.heading: VECTOR UNITS (VU)
rows.label: VU1 Rounding Mode
rows.desc: Determines how the results of floating-point operations are rounded. Some games need specific settings.

rows.heading: VECTOR UNITS (VU)
rows.label: VU1 Clamping Mode
rows.desc: Determines how out-of-range floating point numbers are handled. Some games need specific settings.

rows.heading: VECTOR UNITS (VU)
rows.label: Enable VU0 Recompiler (Micro Mode)
rows.desc: Performs just-in-time binary translation of Vector Unit 0 (VU0) microprograms to native code.

rows.heading: VECTOR UNITS (VU)
rows.label: Enable VU1 Recompiler
rows.desc: Performs just-in-time binary translation of Vector Unit 1 (VU1) microprograms to native code.

rows.heading: VECTOR UNITS (VU)
rows.label: mVU Flag Hack
rows.desc: Good speedup and high compatibility, may cause graphical errors.

rows.heading: VECTOR UNITS (VU)
rows.label: Enable Instant VU1
rows.desc: Runs VU1 instantly. Provides a modest speed improvement in most games. Safe for most games, but a few games may exhibit graphical errors.

rows.heading: ACCURATE FLOATING POINT
rows.label: Accurate FPU Floating Point
rows.desc: Emulates the FPU's floating-point math exactly as the PS2 does, for games whose physics or AI go wrong otherwise. Reduces performance.

rows.heading: ACCURATE FLOATING POINT
rows.label: Accurate VU0 Floating Point
rows.desc: Emulates VU0's floating-point math exactly as the PS2 does. Usually needed together with the FPU option. Reduces performance.

rows.heading: ACCURATE FLOATING POINT
rows.label: Accurate VU1 Floating Point
rows.desc: Emulates VU1's floating-point math exactly as the PS2 does, which fixes some graphical errors. Greatly reduces performance.

rows.heading: I/O PROCESSOR (IOP, MIPS-I)
rows.label: Enable Recompiler
rows.desc: Performs just-in-time binary translation of 32-bit MIPS-I machine code to native code.

rows.heading: GAME SETTINGS
rows.label: Enable Game Fixes
rows.desc: Automatically loads and applies fixes to known problematic games on game start.

rows.heading: GAME SETTINGS
rows.label: Enable Compatibility Patches
rows.desc: Automatically loads and applies compatibility patches to known problematic games.

rows.heading: GAME SETTINGS
rows.label: Apply Recommended Graphics Settings
rows.desc: Applies the higher blending accuracy, accurate alpha test or AA1 that the game database recommends. A game's own settings take priority.

rows.heading: SAVESTATE SETTINGS
rows.label: Create Save State Backups
rows.desc: Creates a backup copy of a save state if it already exists when the save is created. The backup copy has a .backup suffix

rows.heading: SAVESTATE SETTINGS
rows.label: Auto Save State
rows.desc: Automatically saves the game's state at this interval; the pause menu loads it with Load Auto Save. The game may pause briefly while saving.

rows.heading: SAVESTATE SETTINGS
rows.label: Undo Load State
rows.desc: Keeps the game's current state before a save state is loaded, so the pause menu can undo the load.

rows.heading: SAVESTATE SETTINGS
rows.label: Save State for Rest Mode
rows.desc: Saves the game's state when the console's menu is opened and every five minutes, so the game can continue after the console goes into rest mode.

rows.heading: SAVESTATE SETTINGS
rows.label: Compression Method
rows.desc: Sets the compression algorithm for savestate.

rows.heading: SAVESTATE SETTINGS
rows.label: Compression Level
rows.desc: Sets the compression level for savestate.

rows.heading: WHAT CRUX2 WROTE DOWN
rows.label: Current Log
rows.desc: Shows the log of this session.

rows.heading: WHAT CRUX2 WROTE DOWN
rows.label: Save Log
rows.desc: Writes this session's log to "crux2-boot.log", and the rest of the session's lines as they come. For problems that were not detected automatically.

rows.heading: WHAT CRUX2 WROTE DOWN
rows.label: Boot Log
rows.desc: Determines when the boot log is written to "crux2-boot.log". On Error keeps the log in memory and writes it after a crash, a game that failed to start, 15 seconds without a new frame during a game, or Save Log. Always writes every line as it is logged.

rows.heading: WHAT CRUX2 WROTE DOWN
rows.label: Previous Log
rows.desc: Shows the log of the previous session, including a crash report if it crashed.

rows.heading: WHAT CRUX2 WROTE DOWN
rows.label: Emulator Log
rows.desc: Shows the newest lines of PCSX2's log ("logs/emulog.txt").

rows.heading: TAKING THEM ALONG
rows.label: Copy the logs to USB drive 1
rows.desc: Copies the three logs to a folder named "Crux2-logs", to read on a computer or to send with a description of the problem.

rows.heading: LOGGING IN DETAIL
rows.label: File Logging
rows.desc: Writes log messages to emulog.txt.

rows.heading: LOGGING IN DETAIL
rows.label: Verbose Logging
rows.desc: Writes dev log messages to log sinks.

rows.heading: LOGGING IN DETAIL
rows.label: Log Timestamps
rows.desc: Writes timestamps alongside log messages.

rows.heading: LOGGING IN DETAIL
rows.label: EE Console
rows.desc: Writes debug messages from the game's EE code to the console.

rows.heading: LOGGING IN DETAIL
rows.label: IOP Console
rows.desc: Writes debug messages from the game's IOP code to the console.

rows.heading: LOGGING IN DETAIL
rows.label: CDVD Verbose Reads
rows.desc: Logs disc reads from games.

rows.heading: TRACE LOGGING
rows.label: Enable Trace Logging
rows.desc: Globally enable / disable trace logging.

rows.heading: TRACE LOGGING
rows.label: EE BIOS
rows.desc: Log SYSCALL and DECI2 activity.

rows.heading: TRACE LOGGING
rows.label: EE Memory
rows.desc: Log memory access to unknown or unmapped EE memory.

rows.heading: TRACE LOGGING
rows.label: EE GIF Tags
rows.desc: Log GIFtag parsing activity.

rows.heading: TRACE LOGGING
rows.label: EE VIF Codes
rows.desc: Log VIFcode processing; command, tag style, interrupts.

rows.heading: TRACE LOGGING
